events.description: Kabul surrenders to the Taliban; the Taliban and allied jihadists including al-Qaeda enter the capital and prepare to announce the restored Islamic Emirate.
Bin Laden surrounded in Tora Bora; the US relied on outsourced forces and he escaped.
A bin Laden file from mid-2010 recounts Atiyah's report that al-Qaeda had strong military activity across eight Afghan provinces.
Mullah Omar dies of natural causes in mysterious circumstances.
Obama speech announcing an 18-month surge to build up Afghan capacity.
US walks away from peace talks with the Taliban.
US and NATO declare end to combat operations, called a 'big lie' by Roggio.
Trump reluctantly signs off on a strategy to achieve 'victory' in Afghanistan, including a modest troop increase and getting tough on Pakistan.
Trump administration abandons the 2017 strategy and begins negotiations with the Taliban, led by Khalilzad.
US-Taliban withdrawal deal dressed up as a peace deal.
Taliban launches its offensive, taking districts, then provincial capitals; Afghan forces collapse.

key_claims: The Taliban has retaken nearly all of Afghanistan and Kabul has surrendered, with al-Qaeda streaming in alongside it.

Al-Qaeda under bin Laden played a key role in forming the Taliban insurgency; bin Laden files (mid-2010) show strong al-Qaeda military activity across eight provinces, contradicting US claims of only 50-100 fighters.
The December 2001 failure to kill or capture bin Laden at Tora Bora by outsourcing the operation was a fatal strategic mistake.
The 2020 US-Taliban deal was a withdrawal deal dressed up as a peace process that undermined the Afghan government; Taliban district control grew about 80% between February 2020 and May 2021.
Afghan security forces collapsed due to years of failures; the 300,000 figure was a paper army with ghost soldiers, and US officials' timelines kept shrinking.
Successive US presidents from Clinton through Biden made decisions that contributed to the failure; the hosts call for accountability including investigating Khalilzad.
The jihadist threat has been boosted and a new generation of jihadis will emerge from the Taliban victory.
The Afghan security forces were defeated largely between Feb 2020 and May 2021 under the US-Taliban deal, and the collapse had been years in the making.
US leaders' claim of 300,000 capable ANDSF personnel was a paper number that ignored ghost soldiers and hollowing out.
The Taliban never intended a political settlement and the Taliban deal had no enforcement or verification mechanisms.
Sirajuddin Haqqani, the Taliban's number two, is an al-Qaeda man, so Taliban victory is an al-Qaeda victory.
The hosts predict an al-Qaeda moment in Afghanistan where it makes its role clearer.
US officials and generals persistently misread the Taliban and al-Qaeda relationship, from Mattis to Petraeus to Panetta.
